body:
Why natural resources are unevenly distributed

The distribution of natural resources depends on geological structure, climate, soil, relief and water availability. Ancient crystalline regions contain many metallic mineral deposits, while sedimentary basins may contain coal, petroleum and natural gas.

India's mineral-rich regions are concentrated largely in the Peninsular Plateau and associated sedimentary basins. The Chota Nagpur Plateau and adjoining areas of Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal are particularly important.

Major iron ore belts

Iron ore beltStatesImportant locations
Odisha-JharkhandOdisha, JharkhandMayurbhanj, Kendujhar, Noamundi
Durg-Bastar-ChandrapurChhattisgarh, MaharashtraBailadila
Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru beltKarnatakaBallari, Chitradurga, Kudremukh region
Maharashtra-GoaMaharashtra, GoaRatnagiri and Goa mining regions

Iron ore is a basic raw material for the iron and steel industry. The concentration of iron ore and coal deposits in eastern and central India has encouraged the establishment of integrated steel plants.

Other important minerals

MineralImportant geographical locations
BauxiteOdisha's Koraput region; deposits in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
ManganeseOdisha, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
CopperKhetri in Rajasthan; Malanjkhand in Madhya Pradesh; Singhbhum in Jharkhand
Lead and zincZawar and other mining regions of Rajasthan
MicaKoderma region of Jharkhand; Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan
GoldHutti and historical Kolar mining region, Karnataka
LimestoneRajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and other sedimentary regions
Monazite-bearing sandsCoastal regions of southern India, including Keralam and Tamil Nadu

Bauxite is the principal ore of aluminium. Manganese is important in steel production. Limestone is a major raw material in cement manufacturing. Monazite is significant because it contains thorium.

Major coalfields

Coalfield or regionState
Jharia, Bokaro, GiridihJharkhand
RaniganjWest Bengal
TalcherOdisha
KorbaChhattisgarh
SingrauliMadhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
SingareniTelangana
Neyveli lignite fieldTamil Nadu

Many major Indian coalfields occur in Gondwana geological formations. Coal deposits of northeastern India include younger Tertiary formations. Lignite, a lower-rank coal, occurs notably in Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Rajasthan.

Petroleum and natural gas regions

Oilfield or basinGeographical location
Digboi, Naharkatiya and MoranAssam
Mumbai HighOffshore Arabian Sea near Maharashtra
Ankleshwar and KalolGujarat; Cambay basin
Barmer basinWestern Rajasthan
Krishna-Godavari basinEastern coastal and offshore region

An oilfield is a geological region from which crude petroleum is extracted. A refinery processes crude petroleum into useful products. Refineries may be situated far from producing oilfields because crude oil can be transported by pipelines or ships.

Resources of Gujarat

Gujarat contains sedimentary basins with petroleum and natural gas resources, lignite deposits in western regions, limestone deposits and extensive salt-producing landscapes.

  • The Cambay basin is associated with petroleum and natural gas.
  • Kachchh contains lignite, limestone and saline landscapes.
  • Saurashtra and Kachchh contain limestone deposits supporting mineral-based industries.
  • The Rann and coastal regions provide favourable conditions for salt production through evaporation.
  • The western coast and dry interior offer favourable locations for wind and solar energy development.

Important soil and crop regions

Soil or cropImportant geographical region
Alluvial soilNorthern Plains and major river deltas
Black soilDeccan Trap region, including Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh
CottonGujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana and adjoining regions
WheatPunjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
RiceEastern plains, coastal deltas and irrigated agricultural regions
JuteWest Bengal and adjoining eastern regions
TeaAssam, Darjeeling and Nilgiri region
CoffeeKarnataka, Keralam and Tamil Nadu
GroundnutGujarat, especially Saurashtra, and other Peninsular regions

These associations identify major traditional production regions. They should not be interpreted as annual production rankings, which can change with rainfall, cultivation area, prices and agricultural policies.

Prelims focus

  • Bailadila is associated with iron ore in Chhattisgarh.
  • Khetri is associated with copper in Rajasthan.
  • Jharia is a coalfield in Jharkhand.
  • Neyveli is associated with lignite in Tamil Nadu.
  • Ankleshwar is associated with Gujarat's petroleum resources.
  • Trap: Mumbai High is an offshore petroleum field, not a coalfield.

[Sources: NCERT, Class 8, Resources and Development, Mineral and Power Resources; GCERT, Class 8, Social Science, Minerals and Power Resources; NCERT, Class 10, Contemporary India-II, Chapters 1, 4 and 5; NCERT, Class 12, India: People and Economy, Chapter 7, Mineral and Energy Resources, printed pp. 73–84 in the project copy. Online NCERT material used where supporting compendium sections were inaccessible; consulted 27 November 2026.]
title: Natural Resources: Minerals, Energy Resources and Major Agricultural Regions

body:
Geographical factors influencing industrial location

Industries require raw materials, energy, labour, capital, transport and access to markets. Their distribution therefore reflects both physical resources and human economic activity.

Heavy industries that consume large quantities of bulky raw materials often develop near mineral deposits or transport facilities. Industries using imported raw materials may develop near ports. Market-oriented industries may establish themselves near large cities even when local mineral resources are limited.

Major iron and steel centres

Industrial centreState

Jamshedpur, Bokaro, Rourkela, Bhilai and Durgapur are associated with the mineral-rich eastern and central industrial belt. Visakhapatnam is an important example of a coastal steel manufacturing centre.

Other major industrial concentrations

Surat's diamond processing industry is not evidence of major local diamond mining. Diamonds can be imported or transported to centres possessing specialised workers, trading networks and processing facilities.

Alang lies along the western side of the Gulf of Khambhat in the Bhavnagar region. Its ship-recycling activity differs from the petroleum refining and port-based industrial activities associated with the Jamnagar region.

PortStateLocation clue

Major ports along the eastern and southeastern coast

PortStateLocation clue

The term major port identifies an administrative category. It does not necessarily mean that every major port handles more cargo than every non-major port.

Important Gujarat ports by coastal region

RegionImportant ports
Kachchh and northern Gulf of KachchhKandla, Mundra, Mandvi, Jakhau
Southern Gulf of KachchhOkha, Bedi, Sikka, Vadinar
Outer Saurashtra coastPorbandar, Veraval, Pipavav
Gulf of Khambhat regionBhavnagar, Dahej, Hazira

Mundra is a prominent non-major port in Kachchh under the state maritime framework. Deendayal Port at Kandla belongs to the centrally administered major-port system.

Prelims focus

  • Bhilai is in Chhattisgarh; Rourkela is in Odisha.
  • Morbi is associated with ceramics.
  • Alang is associated with ship recycling.
  • Deendayal Port is the renamed Kandla Port.
  • Dahej is associated with the Gulf of Khambhat region.
  • Trap: Mundra and Kandla are distinct ports even though both are situated in Kachchh.

[Sources: NCERT, Class 12, India: People and Economy, Chapter 8, Manufacturing Industries, printed pp. 85–103; NCERT, Class 10, Contemporary India-II, Chapters 6–7; Government of Gujarat industrial cluster identification material reproduced by the Directorate General of Training, Section 7, Clusters for Gujarat; Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Annual Report 2024–25, p. 29, and Ports Wing; Gujarat Maritime Board, port-group listings and Government Gazette, 12 April 2013, Schedule I. Online references consulted 27 November 2026.]
title: Industrial Regions, Manufacturing Centres and Major Ports

body:
Understanding protected-area categories

Protected areas conserve natural habitats, wildlife and ecological processes. Their locations reflect India's varied climates, landforms and vegetation.

A national park is a legally designated protected area with relatively strict protection of its natural environment. A wildlife sanctuary also provides statutory protection to wildlife and habitats, but the treatment of certain existing rights and permitted activities may differ from that in a national park.

A biosphere reserve is a broader conservation landscape that may contain national parks, sanctuaries and areas where compatible human activities occur. A tiger reserve is designated for tiger conservation and may include one or more protected areas. A Ramsar site is a wetland recognised as internationally important under the Ramsar Convention.

These categories can overlap. A single geographical site may be a national park, part of a tiger reserve and part of a biosphere reserve.

Selected biosphere reserves and their locations

Conservation landscapes frequently cross administrative boundaries because ecosystems extend beyond political divisions.

Biosphere reserveState or regional association
NilgiriTamil Nadu, Karnataka and Keralam

Protected-area names, flagship species and geographical locations should be learned together. Gir is associated with the Asiatic lion, Kaziranga with the greater one-horned rhinoceros, Dachigam with the hangul and Keibul Lamjao with the sangai.

Prelims focus

  • Hemis National Park is in Ladakh.
  • Dachigam is associated with the hangul.
  • Kuno National Park is in Madhya Pradesh.
  • Keibul Lamjao is associated with Loktak Lake.
  • The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve extends across 3 southern states.
  • Trap: A Ramsar site is not automatically a national park.

[Sources: NCERT, Class 6, The Earth: Our Habitat, 2018–19 edition, India: Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife, pp. 56–65; NCERT, Class 9, Contemporary India-I, Natural Vegetation and Wildlife; Wildlife Institute of India, state-wise national park and wildlife sanctuary listings; National Tiger Conservation Authority, tiger reserve listings; Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Biosphere Reserves programme. Online sources consulted 27 November 2026. Locations are presented as selected established examples, not an exhaustive current inventory.]
title: National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries and Major Conservation Landscapes
